Impervious taxes could be a viable option to reduce impervious factor: If properly designed it could provide incentives of reducing external impacts through BMPs: While a linear model is easier to translate to tax rates, nonlinear models involved changing tax rates based varying impervious   levels. These   elements need to be practices and for transferability to other watersheds Subsi dies to reduce impervious cover or to incorporate BMPs can also be used to address water quality problems in urbanizing areas. Another incentive policy is cost sharing to encourage adoption of new BMPs or to voluntarily reduce impervious percentage.
